question: Can an agent obtain a new training signal when two existing within-training comparisons share an alternative? In particular, if A defeats B and B defeats C, is the implied ordering borne out on independently recorded direct comparisons?
scope: Inspect only the model refit training payloads of the protected ordinary course preference run and the earlier ordinary movie preference run. Hash both payloads. Normalize alternatives only for equality with the existing shared-text grouper. Record counts, never training text. Synthetic or inferred votes must remain separate from observed labels.
witness: Count directed two-hop paths through three distinct alternatives. Deduplicate raw unordered edges; exclude directions with conflicting labels from witnesses. To evaluate an observed direct comparison never use that direct edge to predict its direction. Keep cycles in evidence, including cases where the path contradicts the direct edge. Each decisive direct edge and inferred pair counts once irrespective of path multiplicity. Report conflicts, ties, independent components and group-bootstrap accuracy interval.
threshold: Register an augmentation experiment only if within that training corpus at least 20 independent components contain a decisive direct-edge witness, its agreement is at least 75% and its group bootstrap 95% lower bound is at least 60%, and unseen directly unlabelled two-hop pairs cover at least 1% of training rows in at least 20 components. No inferred preference or deployable model in this audit. Run the gate separately per corpus and retain negative findings.
usage: Zero supervised fits and zero model API requests. No validation, formal test or H2 inputs or labels.
